newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dairy Farm says less costs to benefit '97.
newsitem.headline: Dairy Farm says less costs to benefit '97.

text.p: Dairy Farm International Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday its 1996 net profit fell to US$27.9 million from US$135.2 million for 1995, but added 1997 will benefit from the absence of non-recurring repositioning costs.
The company said it was "investing for the future" by adapting mature businesses to changing environments and by entering new Asian markets.

"This has inevitably been impacting our results, but we are creating a sound base for renewed profit growth, and in 1997 we will benefit from the absence of non-recurring repositioning costs," Dairy Farm chairman Simon Keswick said in a statement.
It said profit before interest and tax fell to US$90.6 million, down 52 percent.

But the company kept its dividends at the same level as the previous year, recommending a 4.35 U.S. cents final dividend for a full year payout of 6.00 U.S. cents, in consideration of strong cash flow and the outlook for the future.
Profit less dividends for the year was a US$77.4 million loss versus a US$31.7 million profit.
Dairy Farm said Australia and the United Kingdom had produced "poor performances". It said it incurred US$77.5 million in repositioning costs in the two markets.

In Australia it had decided to accelerate the conversion of its Franklin stores' format, while U.K retailer Kwik Save had embarked on a programme to "rationalise and reposition" its stores, which was expected to take three years.
